debate_title: Is current AI progress driven mainly by scaling compute, ...

conflicts.point: Whether software-level cryptographic runtime ledgers can independently and reliably verify AI capability growth without relying on physical infrastructure telemetry.

positions.stance: Cryptographic runtime ledgers on commercial cloud infrastructure verify algorithmic efficiency and capability boundaries without requiring physical power constraints.
Cryptographic ledgers are insufficient alone and must be anchored to physical grid telemetry to prevent evasion through unmonitored software optimization.

conflicts.point: Whether trade policy and export control thresholds should incorporate mandatory labor and environmental standards to address local resource extraction and grid strain.

positions.stance: Export controls should prioritize removing regulatory barriers to rapid algorithmic innovation and medical breakthroughs over managing local resource use.
Trade relief and export frameworks must be tied to enforceable labor and environmental benchmarks to prevent community and ecological harm.

verdicts.conflict: Whether software-level cryptographic runtime ledgers can independently and reliably verify AI capability growth without relying on physical infrastructure telemetry.
verdicts.rationale: The safetyist position relies on verifiable physical metrics like electrical power consumption, which are difficult to spoof. The accelerationist reliance on software runtime ledgers lacks sovereign enforcement authority and leaves major auditing blind spots.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Independent security audits proving that cryptographic runtime ledgers cannot be bypassed by unmonitored software libraries would shift the verdict.

verdicts.conflict: Whether trade policy and export control thresholds should incorporate mandatory labor and environmental standards to address local resource extraction and grid strain.
verdicts.rationale: The accelerationist framework directly addresses the designated Department of Commerce mandate regarding export controls and algorithmic efficiency. The skeptic position broadens the scope into environmental and labor domains that fall outside standard trade enforcement authorities.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Legislative expansion of the Export Control Reform Act to explicitly mandate environmental and labor impact assessments would tip the balance.
